title: Industry Army Marketing Welcomes Fireproofing.tv
excerpt: Introducing Fireproofing.tv: planning education for property owners and building teams, with source-linked guides and clear boundaries between general information and project-specific professional decisions.
intro:
Industry Army Marketing welcomes Fireproofing.tv, an educational publication focused on helping property owners and building teams understand fireproofing before commissioning work. Its starting point is the planning question—not a product recommendation or an installation recipe. The site brings together source-linked guidance for owners, managers and renovation teams who need to frame their next conversation with qualified professionals.

Powered by Industry Army Marketing. A division of BuildersHaus.com.

sections.heading: A publication built around better questions
paragraphs: Fireproofing.tv describes its editorial approach through primary authority, testing and manufacturer sources. Its role is to explain planning decisions while keeping general information separate from matters requiring professional judgment and the relevant local authority. That distinction is central to the welcome: this is an education resource, not a building-certification service.

Readers should approach the library as preparation for a project discussion. Use an article to identify what needs clarification, then take those questions to the people responsible for the building’s design, installation or approval. The publication explicitly does not provide installation instructions or recommend an unreviewed rated assembly.

sections.heading: Start by identifying the protection question
paragraphs: The homepage distinguishes structural protection, penetration firestopping and fire-resistance-rated assemblies rather than treating “fireproofing” as one interchangeable service. Its opening guide maps those different jobs, while another separates fire resistance from flame spread. Together, these topics establish the publication’s practical starting point: first determine which question the project actually needs answered.

The launch library presents 16 starting points. Material-focused subjects include spray-applied fire-resistive materials and intumescent finishes for exposed structural steel. These are framed as planning topics, including understanding a material category before comparing bids and bringing architectural appearance into the design brief.

sections.heading: Prepare the brief before comparing proposals
paragraphs: Several guides address the information surrounding an appointment or estimate. Topics include what to gather before requesting a quote, questions to ask a contractor and why a proposed product needs evidence connecting it to the actual construction. The emphasis is on scope and supporting documents, rather than guessing a price or relying on an unverified badge.

Other planning subjects address environmental exposure and proposed substitutions. For an owner preparing a brief, these headings suggest useful discussion prompts: describe where the steel will be exposed, ask what evidence supports the proposal and request a clear record when the proposed solution changes.

sections.heading: Keep renovation and handover in view
paragraphs: The library also follows questions beyond the initial specification. Renovation topics include adding cables or pipes, service penetrations in mass-timber buildings and conditions that do not match a tested firestop detail. Maintenance coverage includes damaged fireproofing and gaps around fire doors, with the latter directing attention toward the appropriate specialist review.

A separate handover guide focuses on passive fire-protection records that the next building manager can use. For readers, that provides a useful way to organize further questions: what is already documented, what is changing and which concerns need assessment before anyone proposes a repair?

sections.heading: Clear boundaries for participation and enquiries
paragraphs: The contractor page states that applications are not yet open and that the site offers no directory placement, verification badge or approval. It also asks visitors not to send sensitive project records. The welcome should therefore not be read as an invitation to register for a contractor listing.

Commercial and business enquiries belong with Industry Army Marketing through its website; the about page also directs corrections there. Those IAM enquiries are distinct from client requests for project design, installation or approval, which the publication reserves for qualified professionals and the relevant authority. Explore the planning library for education—not as a substitute for that project-specific work.
